source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Exodus 22:1 maps to Hebrew Exod 21:37; public 22:2–31 maps to Hebrew 22:1–30. Chapters 21, 23, and 24 otherwise align.

key_decisions.decision: Names purchased slavery and male referent, preserving six years and seventh-year release without payment.
Preserves the ownership claim and forced family separation rather than presenting this as ordinary employment.
Keeps ha-elohim as God with judicial alternative noted; retains piercing and permanent service without harmonizing to Jubilee.
Keeps daughter-sale and explicit unequal release rule; does not soften female slavery to domestic service.
Follows qere lo for himself rather than written not, records both, and retains redemption and betrayal.
Keeps three obligations and polygynous setting; chooses traditional marital-rights sense of rare onah with uncertainty noted.
Takes three things as preceding obligations and preserves doubled no-payment language.
Retains lack of ambush and explicit divine agency instead of replacing both with a secular accident label.
Keeps deliberate attack with deceitful lethal purpose and removal from altar refuge with execution explicit; avoids making a mere unacted plan the offense.
Unfolds sold or found-in-hand alternatives, keeping human theft and both qualifying outcomes.
Keeps male/female enslaved victims, rod, immediate hand image and vengeance without specifying an unstated penalty.
Retains day-or-two exception and stark monetary-property rationale; does not recast it as benevolent provision or merely financial loss.
Retains children-coming-out idiom and unspecified harm target; judicial oversight follows biflilim without deciding miscarriage versus surviving premature birth.
Keeps unspecified harm and exact reciprocal principle as continuation through the next two verses.
Preserves both enslaved sexes, destroyed eye and freedom as required remedy.
Keeps both sexes, animal execution and meat prohibition, with owner status contextualized to this case.
Preserves prior dangerous behavior plus owner warning and failure, distinguishing culpability from the preceding case.
Preserves unequal fixed payment to the master, exact thirty shekels and animal death; identifies payer and payee clearly.
